plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms including pompons, spiders, and incurves. It is widely grown in gardens and as a cut flower, and it tolerates the cool nights of late fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through late autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide, especially East Asia, Europe, and North America; native to China
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,000 years, and the flower is the symbol of the Japanese Imperial family and of Japan's autumn Chrysanthemum Festival.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, semi-deciduous tree that covers itself in trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before its fern-like leaves fully emerge. In the Southern Hemisphere spring, entire streets turn violet and the fallen blossoms carpet the ground.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina, and Brazil
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because it has tens of thousands of these trees, and a local folk belief says a flower falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in autumn, earlier than the more familiar Camellia japonica. Its delicate, often lightly fragrant single or semi-double flowers provide nectar for pollinators late in the year when little else is in bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter (October to December in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, and the UK
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil, which is used in cooking, cosmetics, and hair care in Japan.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the protea family, made of a ring of showy bracts around a central cluster of tiny florets. It thrives in the nutrient-poor soils of the fynbos and its bloom time stretches into the Southern Hemisphere's late spring and summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere (peaking from October to January, with early blooms in November)
plants.location: Native to the Western Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its thick underground lignotuber lets it resprout after the wildfires that regularly sweep through the fynbos.
